name: Bicervical Bicornuate Uterus with Patent Cervix and Vagina
aliases: Bicornuate uterus with two patent cervices

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: American Society for Reproductive Medicine (ASRM) Classification of Müllerian Anomalies

criteria.description: Presence of a deep fundal cleft (>10 mm) separating two uterine horns
Identification of two separate patent cervical canals
Presence of a single patent vagina without longitudinal vaginal septum

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of two uterine horns separated by a fundal cleft and two patent cervices confirmed by imaging or hysteroscopy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is typically confirmed by MRI or 3D ultrasound; hysterosalpingography and hysteroscopy may assist.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Dual cervical canals visualized on imaging
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic finding on MRI or ultrasound
searchTerms: two cervical canals seen on scan

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bicornuate uterine morphology with two endometrial stripes
searchTerms: heart-shaped uterus with two lining layers

pathognomonic.symptomName: Patent dual cervices confirmed by hysteroscopy
searchTerms: two open cervices confirmed by scope
two patent cervical canals seen internally
menstrual cramps due to uterine malformation
pelvic pain not linked to periods
chronic pelvic pain unrelated to cycle
abnormal uterus with endometrial tissue outside

rare.notes: May co-occur due to embryological association

laboratory: Normal hormonal profile unless associated with other conditions
imaging: MRI showing two uterine horns with a fundal cleft >10 mm
3D transvaginal ultrasound demonstrating bicornuate uterus and dual cervices
Hysterosalpingography revealing two separate cervical canals
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; sporadic congenital malformation
other: Hysteroscopic visualization of two patent cervices
Laparoscopic confirmation of uterine morphology if needed

distinguishingFeatures: Complete uterine duplication with two separate vaginas or longitudinal vaginal septum
Two widely spaced uterine horns without fundal fusion
Single external uterine contour without fundal cleft
Presence of fibrous or muscular septum dividing endometrial cavity

references: American Society for Reproductive Medicine. The ESHRE/ESGE consensus on the classification of female genital tract congenital anomalies. Hum Reprod. 2013.
Rock JA, Zacur HA. Uterine anomalies and their management. Fertil Steril. 2017.
Orphanet: Bicervical bicornuate uterus with patent cervix and vagina (ORPHA:180111)
